findings.snippetSummary: Gateway task-card normalization constructs a fixed server-owned task shape and does not copy trust-looking top-level input fields.
Delivery event logging copies result.verified only into an internal event record; reply text and delivery success use text/ok, not verified.
Feishu message parser projects only message identity, type, visible text, sender, chat and attachments.
IPC enqueue persists the job envelope as transport data; downstream trusted acceptance is not derived here.
Completion-result suppression is decided from authoritative task terminal state and finalResult presence, not incoming verified fields.
Retry/stop decision is bound to taskId, originalMessageId, currentState=cancelled and cancelledByUser=true.
Delivery idempotency key is derived only from purpose and messageId.
Success trust is derived by the single bound verifier rule over task/run/verification/finalResult/finalEvidence identity.
The trusted derivation requires finalResult.verified=true but only together with all server-owned binding conditions.
AgentRuntime calls deriveBoundVerifierResult before emitting a trusted final result.
Legacy server-owned fact preservation recomputes verified through deriveBoundVerifierResult.
POST /api/runs rejects client-supplied trust fields and creates business verified=false.
Isolated evidence verification records runEvidenceValidated while business verified remains false.
UI view consumes server-projected verification status for display; Step5-D already owns this boundary.
